children: Further rate adjustments will likely be needed to ensure that inflation declines to the Federal Reserve's 2% target in a timely fashion, Fed Governor Michael Barr said Wednesday, citing his base case.
The comment comes a week after the Federal Open Market Committee boosted its policy rate by 25 basis points to 3.75%-4.00%, its first rate hike in three years.

"The FOMC took important action to that end last week by increasing the policy rate, which I supported," Barr said in prepared remarks at a Chicago Fed event focused on housing affordability. "In my view, given changes to the economy, we were out of position, and we made an adjustment in the right direction."
Risks to achieving the Fed's inflation target, while risks to the labor market have eased. "We needed to recalibrate monetary policy to reflect the balance of risks to our mandate goals," he said.
